summary: US markets slid Thursday as the Treasury Department's surprise intervention cooled after sparking a Wednesday rally. The Treasury announced it will more than double buybacks of 10-, 20-, and 30-year debt, pushing the 30-year yield down from near 20-year highs above 5.33%, though yields rebounded in Thursday trading. Stocks fell across the board with the Dow down 0.8%, S&P 500 off 0.3%, and Nasdaq sliding 0.8%. President Trump threatened a "crushing economic operation" against Iran, sending oil prices up over 2% and pressuring equities. Meanwhile, Walmart tumbled 9% on slowing US sales growth despite an earnings beat, as customers made "trade-offs" amid high gas prices. Crypto markets surged, with Bitcoin jumping 11.5% to near $71,800 after the Treasury move. Bitcoin ETFs recorded their largest daily inflow since May—$517 million on Wednesday—led by BlackRock's IBIT. The Fed released July FOMC minutes yesterday showing three dissenting members wanted to hike rates, the first three-way hawkish dissent since 2016, underscoring concern about persistent inflation even as the committee held rates at 3.5%-3.75%. Markets now look to Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech next week for clarity on policy direction.

signals.title: Treasury buyback rally fades as bond yields rebound Thursday
signals.desc: Treasury yields reversed Wednesday's sharp decline after the buyback announcement, pressuring stocks lower as the 30-year yield remains near 19-year highs and investors digest the Fed's hawkish July minutes.

signals.title: Trump threatens "crushing" Iran sanctions, oil spikes 2%+
signals.desc: President Trump's social media post vowing economic action against Iran pushed crude oil up over 2%, raising inflation concerns and weighing on equities sensitive to energy costs.

signals.title: Walmart plunges 9% on slowing US sales despite earnings beat
signals.desc: Walmart reported strong earnings but slowing domestic sales growth as customers make "trade-offs" due to high gas prices, dragging consumer discretionary stocks lower and signaling pressure on the lower-income consumer.

signals.title: Bitcoin ETFs post $517M inflow, largest since May 4
signals.desc: US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw their biggest daily haul in over three months led by BlackRock's IBIT, as Bitcoin surged above $69,000 following the Treasury buyback announcement and renewed institutional demand.

signals.title: July FOMC minutes show three members wanted rate hike
signals.desc: Fed minutes released Wednesday revealed the first three-way hawkish dissent since 2016, with members citing persistent inflation concerns and adding uncertainty ahead of Warsh's Jackson Hole speech next week.

verdict: Risk-off tone returns as Treasury relief fades, oil spikes on Iran threats, and hawkish Fed minutes weigh on equities despite crypto's surge.
